Status

FinKore Core 2.0.4 stable.

Purpose

This document defines how FinKore observes an existing Workflow instance with a declared current State and, for versioned instances, a declared Bound Workflow Definition Version.

Import is an observation of existing lifecycle state. It is not a transition, migration, replay, persistence load contract, or authorization check.

Terminology

Workflow Import is the operation that accepts a supplied existing Workflow instance observation and validates it against a supplied Workflow definition.

Imported Current State is the caller-supplied current State for the imported instance.

Imported Workflow Instance Revision is an optional caller-supplied opaque revision of the Workflow instance observation. It supports transition preconditions defined by Workflow Conflicts, but FinKore does not define how it is generated.

Requirements

  • WORKFLOW-IMPORT-001 - Workflow Import MUST use the caller-supplied Imported Current State. It MUST NOT infer the current State from the definition's initial State, declaration order, terminal States, transition history, or implementation defaults.
  • WORKFLOW-IMPORT-002 - Workflow Import MUST validate that the Imported Current State is declared by the supplied Workflow definition or by the supplied Workflow Definition Version for a versioned instance.
  • WORKFLOW-IMPORT-003 - Workflow Import of a versioned instance MUST include exactly one Bound Workflow Definition Version and MUST validate that it exactly matches the supplied Workflow Definition Identity and Workflow Definition Version Identity.
  • WORKFLOW-IMPORT-004 - Workflow Import MUST preserve the supplied Bound Workflow Definition Version and any supplied Imported Workflow Instance Revision as opaque values. It MUST NOT normalize, generate, derive, increment, or reinterpret either value from storage counters, Entity Revision, timestamps, transition counts, or current State.
  • WORKFLOW-IMPORT-005 - A successful Workflow Import MUST return an observation with the supplied current State, Bound Workflow Definition Version when versioned, and Imported Workflow Instance Revision when supplied. It MUST NOT perform a Transition Request, evaluate Transition Guards, create Audit evidence, or claim that a State change occurred.
    Evidence & context1 research note+

    These sources inform discussion of this rule. Their role and limits are stated separately; a citation is not certification or specialist sign-off. Passages from the same study or consultation are not independent confirmation.

    Research / Clarifies a boundary

    Successful import does not authenticate a complete historical record ↗

    László Szívós; István Orosz

    Validation preserves the supplied observation and history; empty supplied history is not historical completeness, and Workflow import creates no transition or Audit evidence. Legacy authentication/reconciliation remains separate.

    Scope and limitations

    A post-migration consistency check can find violated relations but is limited by the predicates and data it covers. Source authentication, omitted history and external reconciliation are separate application responsibilities.

  • WORKFLOW-IMPORT-006 - A failed Workflow Import MUST NOT return a partially imported instance and MUST NOT change any existing Workflow instance observation.

Invariants

Imported instances are observed in their supplied current State. A versioned imported instance is governed by the supplied Bound Workflow Definition Version after validation succeeds.

Errors

Malformed instance observations use FINKORE_WORKFLOW_INVALID_INSTANCE. Undeclared current States use FINKORE_WORKFLOW_INVALID_STATE. Binding mismatches use FINKORE_WORKFLOW_VERSION_MISMATCH. Error precedence is defined by Workflow Errors.

Non-Goals

This document does not define migration between Workflow Definition Versions, state mapping, event replay, Audit provenance, persistence, storage schemas, database locking, distributed concurrency, or actor authorization.
